title: Azuremyst Isle
body: Azuremyst Isle is the southern of the two isles that lie off the northern coast of Kalimdor, a misty country of blue-needled pines, purple blossoms and quiet beaches. In ancient days the night elf empire left it unsettled on purpose, a wild hunting ground, and the ruins of their works still crumble at Wrathscale Point. For centuries its chief inhabitants were the furbolgs of the Stillpine and Bristlelimb tribes. Then the sky caught fire. The Exodar, the dimensional ship the draenei had seized from Tempest Keep, streaked over northern Kalimdor shedding crystals and came down crippled on the western side of the isle. The survivors have made the largest piece of its hull their new home. The crash scattered irradiated crystals across the land, poisoning a lake and maddening beasts and wildkin alike. From the outpost of Azure Watch the draenei work to heal the damage, even as naga, Venture Company goblins and blood elves prowl the island.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Azuremyst_Isle (geography, kaldorei hunting ground, ruins, two furbolg tribes, crash, crystal storm)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Exodar (Velen's raid on Tempest Keep, infiltrated blood elves sabotaged the vessel, shed crystals over northern Kalimdor, crashed on the western side of Azuremyst)

The opening now names only what a newcomer sees: blood elf scouts and bandits. The sabotage itself rests on the wiki, not on the 3.3.5 texts. No era tags: no Wrath-era or patch 2.4 text. Before: Verified. Softened 'edge of the night elf empire' to the wiki's 'left unsettled on purpose', and 'only masters' to 'chief inhabitants' (night elves also lived there). Sabotage claim is TBC-tagged on the wiki (Sunfury). Check: the saboteurs line dropped from part 1: neither trigger shows it (the letter blames the damage on the brutes, the draenei), and exodar.json tells it as the ship's history; part 1 now holds only the letter (Kael'thas, his claim, the assault, the eredar agent).

parts.body: The trouble on the isle ran deeper than it seemed. A letter taken from a traitor showed who stood behind the plotting: Kael'thas Sunstrider, signing himself king, who called the Exodar his own vessel, wanted it repaired, and ordered a full assault on the draenei to take it back. An eredar agent, her identity still unknown to the draenei, had already sent him word of where the ship lay.
sources: page_text 2919-2920 (Traitor's Communication: MY vessel, eredar agent transmitted the Exodar's location, identity still a mystery, full scale assault, repair the Exodar, signed King Sunstrider)

title: Ammen Vale
body: Ammen Vale is a small, hill-sheltered island on the eastern side of Azuremyst, cut off from the rest of the isle by the Crystalbrook River. When the Exodar broke apart, one section of the ship plunged into this valley, and those who woke from long suspension among its wreckage found smoking debris, scattered escape pods and the red glow of irradiated crystals all around them. Many had died. Beside the vale's graveyard a grieving draenei stands over the marker of his beloved Luhanaa, wishing it had been him and swearing vengeance on whoever brought the ship down. A path leads west across the river to Azure Watch, the survivors' road to the rest of their people.

warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Azuremyst_Isle (eastern side is Ammen Vale, sheltered by hills)

title: Crash Site
body: The Crash Site is the broken section of the Exodar that came to rest in Ammen Vale, and it has become the refuge of everyone who lived through the fall. Inside its central chamber the priest Zalduun tends the wounded, while Proenitus rallies those who can still help and Vindicator Aldar sees to the camp's defense. The healing crystals are nearly drained, and the only substitute at hand is the blood of the vale moths, a choice the draenei make with regret, for needless killing is not their way. Technician Zhanaa labors over a damaged holographic emitter, short of spare parts, in the hope of finding other survivors beyond the vale.

quest 9409 (Zalduun tending the wounded inside the central chamber)

parts.body: In time the emitter did its work. Word from Zhanaa reached Azure Watch across the Crystalbrook, and the two camps found each other: survivors still lived in Ammen Vale, and their kin were waiting beyond the river.

title: Silverline Lake
body: South of the Crash Site, Silverline Lake took one of the Exodar's power crystals straight into its waters. The irradiated crystal poisoned the lake, and the plants and animals that drank from it began to change. Mutated root lashers now choke the Ammen Fields to the west, the breeding ground of the vale's lashers, where flowers bloom an unnatural red, and strange volatile creatures have sprung up near the fallen power cores. Botanist Taerix has a theory on how the lake might be healed, if only she can study samples taken from the mutated lashers.
sources: quest 9293 description (lake contaminated by a power crystal, mutated lashers in the Ammen Fields to the west)
quest 9294 description and reward text (lake to the south, neutralizing agent, unsure how long it will last, crystal should be removed)
quest 9799 (Ammen Fields primary breeding ground of lashers, corrupted red flowers)

parts.body: Taerix's theory held. From the samples she devised a neutralizing agent, and once it was scattered beside the crystal the poison seemed to lift. No one knows how long it will last, and Taerix wishes the crystal could be pulled from the lake entirely.

title: Nestlewood
body: The wooded thickets and hills of Nestlewood, south of the Crash Site, are home to the Nestlewood owlkin. Many were twisted by the contamination from the crash and turned violent, while others remain untouched. Rather than wipe out the flock, the draenei carry an inoculating crystal prepared by Botanist Taerix to shield the healthy birds, and put down only those already too far gone. The owlkin had also carried off devices salvaged from the ship, and Technician Zhanaa needed those parts to repair her emitter. The inoculated birds take the crystal in very different ways: some seem overjoyed, some confused, and some plainly did not like what just happened.

title: Shadow Ridge
body: Shadow Ridge rises beyond Silverline Lake on the southwestern edge of Ammen Vale. The survivors believed their scouting of the vale complete, yet reports of unusual activity on the ridge keep reaching the Crash Site, and one scout, Tolaan, has not come back. Blood elves have made camp along it. Their scouts patrol the slopes, vowing that no survivor will leave the valley alive, and a surveyor named Candress keeps to their camp.

parts.body: Tolaan was found on the ridge, gravely wounded and barely able to speak. Blood elves had ambushed him, and with what breath he has left he urges that the threat on the ridge be dealt with before it reaches the survivors.

The orders Surveyor Candress carried told what the party was for: survey the extent of the islands and report back, and on no account be caught. They were signed with a single letter, S. The blood elves had followed the draenei all the way to Azeroth.

title: The Sacred Grove
body: Nestled in the hills of northwestern Ammen Vale, the Sacred Grove is the home of the Spirit of the Vale. The violent arrival of the draenei threw the elements here out of balance: the enraged spirits of earth turned on the spirits of air, fire and water that came to calm them, and the grove is still a battlefield. The spirit has little love for the newcomers, yet it receives the draenei shaman who seek it, teaching that earth is the foundation on which all other elements rest. Shamanism is only now being relearned among the draenei, and many of their people distrust it, so a balance struck here is a hopeful sign.

title: Azure Watch
body: Azure Watch is the outpost the Hand of Argus raised in the forest west of the Crystalbrook, within sight of the wrecked Exodar. Exarch Menelaous commands it, and its artificers, healers and trainers serve the many injured draenei who pass through. Technician Dyvuun works an emitter here in the hope of reaching survivors elsewhere on the isle, and a mysterious guest, a night elf found unconscious by the river, lies here in the care of its healers. A furbolg, Arugoo of the Stillpine, waits in the village beside a carved totem, whose symbols the cryptographer Aurren believes hold the key to speaking with the Stillpine tribe.

title: Moongraze Woods
body: North of Azure Watch, Moongraze Woods is home to herds of moongraze stags and bucks. Draenei hunters say the stags recall the talbuk their greatest hunters stalked on Draenor, though one draenei youngling out on the hunt grumbles that the two look nothing alike. The woods also hide a darker problem. Infected nightstalker runts prowl among the trees, and the sickened beasts behave strangely, though what ails them cannot be seen from the outside.

quests 9455, 9456 (crystal in a nightstalker runt, crystal fragments in the river to the east, this is clearly our fault)

parts.body: The cause lay in their bellies. A runt was found with a faintly glowing crystal inside it, a piece of the Exodar, and Exarch Menelaous admitted the fault was his people's: reports of crushed crystal in the river to the east had been ignored too long. He has ordered the infected nightstalkers culled before the contamination spreads any further.

title: Emberglade
body: On the island's northeast coast lies Emberglade, a sacred place of fire where scorched trees stand above smoldering ground and flaming aspects drift between them. Its guardian is Temper, a fire elemental of great power, who teaches that flame is renewal as well as destruction: it consumes what it burns, then dies, to be reborn another time. The crash of the Exodar unbalanced one of Temper's own kind, Hauteur, who has gone mad and set himself up as a god among the owlbeasts, a thing no true elemental would do. Draenei shaman come here to be tested before shaping their first fire totems.
sources: quest 9464 (sacred place of fire to the northeast on the coast, burned trees, Temper a fire elemental of great power)
quest 9465 description and reward text (Hauteur gone insane because of the crash, flame consumes then dies to be reborn)

parts.body: Temper's teaching proved true of Hauteur himself. Slain beside the effigy his worshippers burned for him, the mad elemental was reborn from his own ashes, and he now burns beside Temper at Emberglade, brighter than ever before and, it seems, a little reluctant to speak.

title: Stillpine Hold
body: Stillpine Hold is the cave home of the Stillpine furbolgs in the north of the isle, ruled by High Chief Stillpine. For centuries the tribe lived at peace with the creatures of the land, until the crystal storm fell from the sky. Then the wildkin, once their allies, went mad and stormed the hold with a beast of legend, the Kurken, at their side. Now the tribe holds only the ground before its own cave. Stillpine the Younger, heir to the tribe's legacy, has set a death trap for the raving wildkin that pour out, and the bodies of defenders and wildkin lie where they fell. Why the wildkin turned is a question the high chief wants answered.

parts.body: Deep inside the hold lay the answer: a crystal from the Exodar, blood red and rapidly dissolving into the water supply of the cave, radiating a sickly aura. Something has gone terribly wrong with it, and it may explain why the creatures of Azuremyst have turned so savage.
With the Kurken slain, High Chief Stillpine declares the hold saved. His people will soon make their way back to their ancestral home, and he hails a new age of prosperity for the Stillpine.
sources: quest 9622 description (the Hold is saved, return to the ancestral home)

title: Menagerie Wreckage
body: Along the northeast beaches lie the shattered cages of the Exodar's menagerie, scattered there when the ship came down. Ravagers were carried aboard as specimens, and with their cages broken the insect-like predators have spread into the forest. The Stillpine had never seen such creatures, and when ravagers ambushed two furbolg hunters, the leatherworker Moordo wondered aloud whether they heralded the end of the world. One of the deadliest, a death ravager, was still caged nearby, little armored but resistant to most magic, and draenei warriors were sent to free it from its prison and its pain with a plain blade. Blood elf bandits also lurk among the wreckage.

title: Silting Shore
body: The Silting Shore on the northwest coast belongs to the Siltfin murlocs. The Stillpine never trusted them, but in these dark days the murlocs have grown bold enough to raid Stillpine Hold and carry off its grain. One of them humiliated the furbolg Gurf in broad daylight, kicking him and spitting on him, and Gurf would dearly like news of a dark-skinned murloc with a patch of white fur stuck between its toes. A darker presence haunts these beaches too. A quel'dorei magewraith, a spirit consumed by its own magic, rises when spells are hurled carelessly along the shore, and draenei mages are sent to face it as a lesson in self-control.

parts.body: The culprit was Murgurgula, the fearsome brute of the Siltfin. When he fell, the white fur between his toes was found to be a clump of Gurf's own, 'lost' in his struggle with the murlocs, and so what remained of Gurf's dignity could at last be carried home to him.

title: Bristlelimb Village
body: Deep in the western woods, reached by an ancient elven road, stands Bristlelimb Village, home of the Bristlelimb furbolgs. The two furbolg tribes of the isle are at war, and the totems of the Stillpine record terrible deeds done to them by the Bristlelimb. Cages throughout the village hold Stillpine captives, and their captors, from hulking ursa to windcallers, hold the keys. The furbolg language totem that stands here bears the word vark, which means justice, and its carvings foretell a hero, not of furbolg blood, who will rise to save the Stillpine.

title: Odesyus' Landing
body: Odesyus' Landing is an Alliance camp on the southern shore of Azuremyst, set up by Admiral Odesyus of Alliance Naval Command after goblin stowaways forced his two ships into port. Loggers and axemen work the nearby forest while Stormwind marines stand guard. The camp gathers an unlikely company: 'Cookie' McWeaksauce, a reformed pirate whose menu so often comes down to chicken that the admiral dreads asking about dinner; the dwarf Adamant Ironheart of the Explorers' League; the night elf Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare; and a gnome engineer, Spark Overgrind, an envoy of High Tinker Mekkatorque who passes his days collecting shells along the beach.

title: Geezle's Camp
body: East of Odesyus' Landing, Venture Company goblins have pitched a camp of their own in the thicket, under a boss named Geezle. They reached Azuremyst hidden in the holds of the admiral's ships, struck one night while the crew slept below deck, and jumped ship with the fleet's compass and charts. Saboteurs and gemologists now keep the camp, and the stolen gear lies somewhere among their tents.

parts.body: Rolled inside the stolen map were orders from Mogul Razdunk, and they were blunt: strip-mine the island of the Exodar's crystal wreckage, then hijack the Alliance ships once the work was done. The goblins knew far too much of the admiral's plans, and the papers left him sure that someone in his own crew was in league with them.

title: Wrathscale Point
body: West of Odesyus' Landing lie the remains of an ancient night elf settlement, long abandoned and now overrun by the Wrathscale naga. Myrmidons and sirens prowl among the broken stones, and relics of the old kaldorei lie buried all through the ruins. On the coast nearby the naga also hold a cave, Tides' Hollow. Some of the naga carry tablets covered in runes. To Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare these are the lands of her ancestors, and she will not see them tainted.

title: Silvermyst Isle
body: Silvermyst Isle lies a short way off the southwest coast of Azuremyst. For years the night elf fisherman Cowlen lived here with his wife and daughter, at peace with the owlbeasts of the island. When crystal shards from the Exodar fell here, the owlbeasts of Moonwing Den went mad. With murlocs beside them they stormed the beach, razed Cowlen's home and sank his ship, leaving him alone on the docks. Deranged and raving owlbeasts still fill Moonwing Den, and there the mad fire elemental Hauteur commanded them to burn an effigy in his honor and worship him as their god.

title: Valaar's Berth
body: Valaar's Berth is the dock on Azuremyst's western shore, south of the Exodar, where the ship Elune's Blessing comes in from Auberdine on the Darkshore coast. For the draenei it is the door to the rest of Kalimdor and to the allies they hoped to find there. For travelers sailing the other way, it is a first glimpse of the strangers who fell from the sky. Beyond the pier, skittering crawlers pick their way along the sand.

title: Exarch Menelaous
body: Exarch Menelaous commands Azure Watch, the draenei outpost within sight of the wreck of the Exodar. Gazing at the broken ship, he says it is hard to imagine that anyone survived such a catastrophe. He speaks of ten lifetimes spent fleeing the madness of the Burning Legion, and swears that here at last the draenei will stop running and make their stand, though he is ready to die for it, for the Prophet holds that it is here their fate will finally be known. Reports of trouble from every corner of the isle cross his desk, and those that matter go on to Velen.
sources: npc_text of Exarch Menelaous 17116 (ten lifetimes fleeing the Legion, no more running, I am ready to die)
quest 9616 reward text (bounty on draenei, Velen will be informed)
quest 9602 reward text (spy, will notify Velen)
notes: Converted: his admission over the crystals moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9455); the bounty to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9616); the gnome traitor and the spy to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9602). Opening is now his gossip (npc_text 8806). Dialogue check: npc_text 8806 and 9040 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified; 'nearest' unsupported, changed to 'within sight' (his gossip: gaze upon the Exodar). Faction 1: template 1638 has the Horde as enemy group.

parts.body: When a crystal from the Exodar turned up inside a sickened nightstalker, Menelaous made no excuses. Reports of crushed crystal fragments in the river to the east had been ignored, he admitted, and the fault was his people's. Rather than sit and mourn the harm done to the land, he ordered the infected beasts culled before it could spread.

A ledger taken from blood elf bandits showed a price on draenei heads, drawn as a slain draenei with a smiling elf standing over the corpse. By the beardless, geometric head of O'ros, the exarch swore: these blood elves are out for blood, and Velen will be told at once.
sources: item 23910 drops from Blood Elf Bandit 17591

parts.body: Worse news came from Odesyus' Landing: a letter taken from a gnome traitor in the service of Kael'thas. Reading it, Menelaous cursed them all to the Nether, for it showed that a spy had been watching everything the draenei did, for who knows how long. He took the warning straight to Velen.

title: Vindicator Aldar
body: Vindicator Aldar watches over the survivors at the Crash Site in Ammen Vale. He tells young draenei that the Light offers many paths, and that each of them must choose which to walk on this world or any other. He set the vale's first recovery in motion, sending helpers to inoculate the owlkin around the salvage and scouts up to Shadow Ridge, where reports of unusual activity trouble him, for one of his scouts has not reported back.
sources: npc_text of Vindicator Aldar 16535 (many are the paths of the Light)
quest 9798 reward text (blood elves followed us, evil to the core, apology)
notes: Converted: his reaction to the surveyor's death moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9311, new detail from its completion text); the outburst over the plans to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9798). Opening keeps the missing scout as the situation (quest 9309). Dialogue check: npc_text 8616 holds nothing from later builds. Before: Verified; 'scouts out to the hills' corrected to Shadow Ridge (quest 9309). Faction 1: template 1638.

parts.body: Then it was true: a scouting party of blood elves in Ammen Vale itself. With their surveyor slain, Aldar promised to deal with whatever remnant of them was still nearby and sent for Tolaan to be brought back, but he could not understand how the sin'dorei had followed his people so far.

The plans taken from the surveyor broke his composure. The blood elves have followed us here, he cried; they are evil to the core and should be wiped from existence. Then he caught himself and apologized, a rare crack in a vindicator's discipline.

title: Admiral Odesyus
body: Admiral Odesyus of Alliance Naval Command was at sea with two ships when goblin stowaways struck one night, stole his navigation gear and jumped ship, forcing him into port on Azuremyst. Embarrassed even to speak of it, he has made camp on the southern shore, and help in getting his compass and charts back would, he says, make for a strong gesture. Between crises he trades weary banter with his cook, whose grand promises for dinner always end in chicken, and he assures his helpers that he is taking care of everything.
sources: quest 9506 description and reward text (both ships, navigation gear, off course, I smell a traitor)
quests 9530, 9531 (none of my crew can be trusted, tree disguise)
creature_text 17240 and 17246 (dinner banter, it be chicken)
notes: Converted: the goblins' purpose, his suspicion and the tree scheme moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9506); the traitor's identity to a new part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9531). Opening adds his gossip (npc_text 8865). Dialogue check: npc_text 8864, 8865, 8892, 9038 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified. Faction 1: template 12 hostile to the Horde.

parts.body: The theft was no prank. Orders found rolled in the map showed the goblins meant to strip-mine the island's crystal wreckage and then seize his fleet, and the admiral smelled a traitor: only someone close to him could have told them his plans. Trusting none of his crew, he turned to newcomers on the isle and devised an absurd scheme involving a hollowed-out tree and a pile of leaves.

The scheme worked. Disguised as a tree, an observer watched the goblin boss meet his contact, and the admiral could hardly believe the answer: it was the gnome all along, the envoy of Mekkatorque. If so high an official of the Alliance could turn traitor, he wondered, how many others might be corrupt?

title: Engineer Spark Overgrind
body: Engineer Spark Overgrind came to Azuremyst as an envoy of High Tinker Mekkatorque, sailing with Admiral Odesyus, and he now waits at Odesyus' Landing while the admiral's ships sit in port. He passes his days hunting seashells along the beach, examining each find, holding the biggest to his ear and tucking them into his pack, and he confesses that he hates the ocean but loves the beach. Those who interrupt him are told he is busy.
sources: creature_text 17243 (seashells, meeting with Geezle, Velen left open, the Legion's servants, die by the will of Kael'thas)
quest 9531 reward text (it was the gnome)
page_text 2919-2920 (Kael'thas: MY vessel, only link able to repair the Exodar)
notes: Converted: the opening told everything; it now holds only what meeting him, or any bystander at his death, shows (the envoy, the shells, creature_text 17243 groups 11-12, gossip npc_text 8978). The traitor reveal at the meeting moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9531); his unmasking, death and the letter to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9537). KILL 17243 is kept as an entry trigger only: a Horde character can kill him without the gossip-started confrontation (actionlist 1724300) and so hears none of it. Added TALK 17243 (gossip menu 7426, Alliance only) so the opening can be met before the chain. Faction stays 0. Before: Verified. Faction 0: template 875 has the Horde as enemy group and unit_flags 37376 carry no IMMUNE_TO_PC, so a Horde character can attack him; he has one permanent spawn at Odesyus' Landing (3573), and Azuremyst has no faction phasing in 3.3.5. QUEST_DONE 9531 is Alliance only but is not the only route. Check: TALK 17243 kept: the original triggers are all still there, the opening is now safe for anyone who meets him, and TALK is the brief's trigger for a friendly NPC (faction 875, gossip 7426, hostile to the Horde, so the Horde still unlocks only by KILL). The opening holds for a Horde killer: the envoy subname, the shells and the beach lines (creature_text groups 11-12) are seen by anyone near him; the confrontation script (1724300) is gossip-only behind quest 9537.

parts.body: His beachcombing was a cover. Spark was the traitor in league with the Venture Company. At a secret meeting at a cove in the west, marked by a naga flag, he berated their boss Geezle for leaving the stolen compass and charts in plain view, spoke of a spy on the inside, warned what Kael'thas does to those who fail him, and boasted that Velen would soon leave himself open to attack.

Unmasked on the beach, Spark laughed, and taunted that devoted servants of the Legion live quietly within every civilization until they are called upon. Live in fear, die by the will of Kael'thas, he said, and drew his blade. He fell fighting, and a letter on his body showed that Kael'thas meant him to repair the Exodar and return it to its self-proclaimed owner.

title: Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare
body: Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare is a night elf servant of Elune staying at Odesyus' Landing, and she makes no secret of her suspicion of the draenei. Her people, she says, know much of the newcomers' forebears, and in appearance they resemble the eredar far too closely. Still, she senses that fate has pushed them all toward this island for a reason. The ruins to the west were once the lands of her ancestors, and she cannot bear to see them fouled by the Wrathscale naga, whose kind she has seen at their worst.
sources: npc_text of Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare 17241 (eyes you suspiciously, similarities to the eredar, tenuous path)
quest 9513 (invisible hand of fate, ancestral lands, Elune be praised)
quest 9515 description and reward text (I've seen what naga can do, I was wrong to think badly of you, Archimonde, gift from the night elves)
notes: Converted: her change of heart moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9515). Dialogue check: npc_text 8861-8863, 8893 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified. Faction 1: template 80.

parts.body: Once Warlord Sriss'tiz was dead, Kyleen's doubts gave way. The threat of a naga invasion is only a distant memory now, she says, and the isle is safe, for the time being. She admits she was wrong to think badly of the draenei, who show nothing of the filth that was Archimonde, and offers them a gift from the night elves.

title: Archaeologist Adamant Ironheart
body: Adamant Ironheart of the Explorers' League is a dwarf of Ironforge who once served in its elite guard, and he will tell anyone who listens that he was Magni's right-hand man. Retired now, he took up archaeology as a hobby and a fine excuse to see the world. His pappy always said that where there are night elf ruins, night elf relics are sure to be close by, so the ruins at Wrathscale Point thrill him, and he promises his diggers that Ironforge will hear all about them.
sources: npc_text of Adamant Ironheart 17242 (Ironforge elite guard, Magni's right hand man, retired, archaeology hobby)
quest 9523 description and reward text (pappy, relics, they'll learn about you in Ironforge)
creature_text 17242 (Anything for you, darling; reads the tablet)
notes: Converted: the tablet scene, and with it his gallantry toward Kyleen, moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9514). Dialogue check: npc_text 8867, 8868, 8892 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified. Faction 1: template 55.

parts.body: When Priestess Kyleen brought him a rune covered tablet, he answered with gallantry, 'anything for you, darling', and read it slowly in the naga's own tongue. Naga warlord, he groaned, and told her she would not like it: Warlord Sriss'tiz had ordered his naga to take the rest of the island by force, with reinforcements coming from Nazjatar.

title: High Chief Stillpine
body: High Chief Stillpine rules the Stillpine furbolgs of Azuremyst. His tribe lived in peace with the creatures of the land for centuries, until the omens of Kurz the Revelator warned that the gods would shatter the land and turn friend and foe alike against the Stillpine, and that a hero not of Stillpine blood, the Promised One, would deliver them. Then the crystal storm came, and the maddened wildkin drove his people out of their own hold. His first concern is the root of that corruption, and he sends the Promised One into the cave to find it.
sources: quest 9559 reward text (centuries of peace, Kurz's dark omens, gods would shatter the land, the Promised One)
quest 9622 (hold saved, people return to their ancestral home, darkness looms for your people, aid of the Stillpine)
notes: Converted: the hold saved, his warning and his pledge moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT or QUEST_DONE 9622). Dialogue check: npc_text 8983, 8997, 9039 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified; the pledge of aid in 9622 is made to the Promised One, not to the draenei as a whole, so reworded. Faction 1: template 1685 has the Horde as enemy group.

parts.body: With the hold saved, his people can make their way back to their ancestral home, and he hails a new age of prosperity for the Stillpine. Yet he warns that darkness looms ahead for the draenei, with questions left unanswered, and he promises the Promised One the tribe's aid whenever it is asked for.

title: Kurz the Revelator
body: Kurz the Revelator is the seer of the Stillpine. Several months ago he began to see dark omens of a catastrophe that would end the tribe's long peace, and of a hero not of Stillpine blood who would rise to deliver them. When the crystal storm had passed, a beast of myth called the Kurken came into the village with the invading wildkin and slew many furbolgs who tried to stand against it. Kurz has seen in his visions the one who will bring it down, and he greets the draenei champion as the Promised One.
sources: quest 9559 reward text (several months ago Kurz began to see dark omens, hero not of Stillpine blood)
quest 9570 description and reward text (crystal storm, the Kurken, I have seen one defeat the Kurken)
npc_text of Kurz 17443 (the Promised One has arrived)
quest 9622 reward text (they saw the power core of the Exodar and O'ros)
notes: Converted: the Kurken's fall moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9570, new from its reward text); the visions of the core and O'ros to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9622, where Menelaous hears of them). Dialogue check: npc_text 8983, 8994 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified; 'months before the draenei arrived' was an inference, now the quest's 'several months ago'. Vision of the core and O'ros credited to the tribe (9622), not Kurz alone. Faction 1: template 1685. Check: part 2: 'which the tribe asked to be carried back' softened (the chief only says to tell your leaders what you have seen).

parts.body: His vision held true. The Kurken fell in the depths of Stillpine Hold, and when its hide was brought to him, Kurz proclaimed that the Promised One had emerged victorious and that the prophecy was nearly complete, then turned at once to the matter of the beast's hide.

The prophecy has come to pass, but the visions of the Stillpine have shown something stranger still, and word of it was carried back to the draenei: the power core of the Exodar, and the naaru O'ros. What it means, not even Exarch Menelaous can say.

title: Warlord Sriss'tiz
body: Warlord Sriss'tiz leads the Wrathscale naga who have overrun the night elf ruins of Wrathscale Point on Azuremyst's southern coast. While his myrmidons and sirens prowl the broken stones above, he keeps to Tides' Hollow, a cave along the coast to the west of Odesyus' Landing, and lashes out with watery strikes at any who come close. To Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare, the ruins his naga hold are the lands of her ancestors.
sources: creature_text 17242 (tablet: Sriss'tiz ordered his naga to take the rest of the island by force, reinforcements from Nazjatar)
notes: Converted: the opening told his orders, which a group member at the KILL 17298 need never have read; it now holds what such a bystander sees (the warlord in his cave, his Watery Strike, smart_scripts 17298) and what the Wrathscale Point opening tells. The tablet's plan and Kyleen's fear moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9514 or QUEST_ACCEPT 9515); his death to part 2 (KILL 17298 or QUEST_DONE 9515), told as a bystander sees it. Before: Verified. Faction 0: template 74 is hostile to all players, single permanent spawn; ACCEPT 9515 is Alliance only but KILL is open to both. Tides' Hollow per wiki and spawn position. Check: part 1 trigger narrowed to QUEST_ACCEPT 9515: Kyleen's fear is told only in 9515's description, and 9515 needs 9514, so its accept also covers the tablet. Watery Strike (smart_scripts 17298, spell 31275) confirmed; Tides' Hollow: the AreaTable 3569 cell lies about 90 yards from his underground spawn, with naga spawned around him, matching 9515's coastal cave to the west.

parts.body: Orders carried by his warriors laid out his ambition: to take the rest of the island by force, with more naga coming from Nazjatar to swell his ranks. Priestess Kyleen, who has seen what naga can do, fears an invasion would be a catastrophe for every being on the isle, and wants the warlord's reign ended before his reinforcements arrive.

Sriss'tiz fell at last in the depths of Tides' Hollow, struck down in the cave where he had kept himself hidden. Whatever he planned for Azuremyst, the Wrathscale who hold the ruins above have lost their warlord.

title: Survivors of the Crash
body: Weeks after the Exodar fell, the last draenei lying in suspension in Ammen Vale began to wake to a ruined world. Proenitus, unsure why the ship crashed, knows only that there is little time to save whoever can still be saved. The healing crystals are spent, and the only substitute at hand is the blood of the vale moths, an unhappy necessity for a people who shun needless killing. The vials go to the priest Zalduun, who sends the able out to find the injured by the red glow of crystal radiation and heal them with the gift of the naaru. Botanist Taerix wants the volatile creatures near the fallen cores culled and the mutated lashers studied, hoping to heal the poisoned lake. Travelers of the Alliance who reach the vale are pressed into the same work.
sources: quest 9369 AllowableRaces 77 (human, dwarf, night elf, gnome)
notes: Converted: the rescued survivors moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9283, draenei only, since healing uses the Gift of the Naaru); the neutralizing agent to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9294, open to every Alliance race). Opening trimmed to the Story range. Before: Verified; Taerix asked others to cull the mutations (10302), reworded. Faction 1: 9279 draenei only, 9369 other Alliance races. Check: part 2's last line (apprentices, sent on to Aldar) came from 10304's description, which turning in 9294 does not show; replaced with Tedon from 9294's reward text.

parts.body: One by one the survivors were found and healed. They stagger up asking where they are and what became of the ship, or remembering only the fall and the scramble for the pods, then go to help the others. Zalduun praised the work as only a true hero could have done it.

Taerix's study gave her an answer: a neutralizing agent, scattered beside the crystal in Silverline Lake. It worked, though she cannot say for how long, and she wishes the crystal could be removed entirely. Meanwhile she would have Tedon try the agent on one of the captured beasts at once.

title: The Blood Elves of Shadow Ridge
body: Even as survivors gather at the Crash Site, reports of strange activity on Shadow Ridge keep reaching Vindicator Aldar, though his people believed their scouting of the vale thorough. One of his scouts, Tolaan, has not come back, and Aldar sends help southwest across Silverline Lake to find him and learn what has delayed him. The survivors are few and battered, and they need time: time to tend their wounded and to repair the emitter that may yet reach other draenei beyond the vale.
sources: quests 9309, 10303, 9311 descriptions, reward and completion texts
creature_text 17268 and 16551 (Zhanaa and Dyvuun on the emitter)
notes: Converted: Tolaan's ambush moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9309); Candress's death and Aldar's reaction to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9311); her orders to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT or QUEST_DONE 9798, also an entry trigger); the emitter to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 9312, which follows 9311). KILL 16522 not used: the plans and Aldar's words are not seen at the fight. Before: Verified. Faction 1: both quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Tolaan was found on the ridge, gravely wounded and barely able to speak: blood elves had ambushed him. A whole party of their scouts holds the ridge, determined that no draenei will leave the vale alive, and with what strength he has left Tolaan urges that their numbers be thinned.

Thinning them was not enough, so Tolaan urged that their leader, Surveyor Candress, be slain, in the hope that the rest would pull back and buy time for the repairs. Candress died refusing to be taken alive. Aldar could not understand how the sin'dorei had followed his people so far, and promised to deal with whatever was left of them.
sources: quest 9311 description, completion and reward text

parts.body: The orders Candress carried, signed with a single letter, S., showed why the party had come: to survey the extent of the islands and report back, and on no account to be caught.

Soon after, the repairs were done. Technician Zhanaa's emitter flickered to life, and a faint, crackling voice answered her from beyond the Crystalbrook: Technician Dyvuun, at Azure Watch. Their kin beyond the vale were alive.

title: The Sleeping Priestess
body: A night elf priestess was found injured and unconscious beside the Crystalbrook only the day before, and carried to Azure Watch, a delicate guest among so many injured draenei passing through that healing ointments are always in short supply. Anchorite Fateema has found that the vines of the island's lashers hold restorative properties, and believes that with proper treatment they can be broken down into an ointment strong enough to save her. There is little time to lose, for Fateema fears that the priestess's health is in steady decline.
sources: quest 9505 reward text (Odesyus: one of our crew)
notes: Converted: the failed ointment moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9463); her waking and the Prophet's words to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9473); the admiral's recognition to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9505). Opening ends on what stays true: the healers have never seen a night elf (creature_text 17215, 17587). Before: Verified. Faction 1: 9463 is draenei only. Check: opening's last line (healers have never seen her kind) was not supported and would go stale once the admiral names her; replaced with 9463's 'found only yesterday', 'delicate guest' and completion text 'health in steady decline'. Part 1 now QUEST_ACCEPT 9473 (the snapdragon is 9473's description; turning in 9463 shows only the failed ointment); part 2 now QUEST_ACCEPT 9505 (the Prophet's words and the messenger are 9505's description; turning in 9473 shows only the waking). Each accept needs the turn-in before it.

parts.body: The ointment was not enough. Fateema applied it to the priestess's wounds and found it ineffective, and the alchemist Daedal turned instead to the azure snapdragon, a rare bloom some call a cure for every ill, which grows at the foot of the island's azure pines and is eaten by the root threshers.
sources: creature_text 17214, smart_scripts 1721400 (ointment ineffective, on turning in 9463)

parts.body: The remedy roused her, briefly. The priestess sat up, saw who stood around her and cried out against cursed eredar, warning that she had not come alone, before slipping back into her coma. To be taken for the man'ari stung the draenei deeply. Daedal remembered words of the Prophet: on this island their allies would find them, but they would be tested and asked to pay for the sins of their fathers. He sent a messenger south to find her people.
sources: creature_text 17117, 17214, 17215, smart_scripts 1721500 (the waking, on turning in 9473)

parts.body: The messenger found them at Odesyus' Landing on the southern shore, where Admiral Odesyus recognized the sleeping priestess as one of his own crew and sent a crewman to Azure Watch at once to see to her.

title: The Traitor of Odesyus' Landing
body: Admiral Odesyus of Alliance Naval Command has a problem he finds embarrassing even to talk about. Venture Company goblins stowed away in the holds of both his ships, struck one night while most of the crew slept below deck, and jumped ship with his compass and charts, forcing him into port on Azuremyst. They vanished into the thicket east of his camp, and the admiral asks any willing stranger to go after the stolen gear, for it would make a strong gesture.
sources: DB: naga flag object 181694 at Traitor's Cove (posarea 3579)
notes: Converted: Razdunk's orders and the traitor suspicion moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9506); the meeting and Spark's identity to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9531); his death and the letter to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9537); Menelaous and Velen to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 9602). Before: Verified. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Rolled inside the recovered map were orders from Mogul Razdunk: strip-mine the island's crystal wreckage, then hijack the Alliance ships. The goblins knew too much, and the admiral concluded that someone close to him had sold him out. Trusting no one in his crew, he called for a hollowed-out tree and a pile of leaves.

The tree was a disguise. Wearing it at a cove in the west where a naga flag marked a secret meeting, a spy hidden in plain sight watched Geezle meet his contact: Spark Overgrind, envoy of Mekkatorque and servant of Kael'thas, who boasted that Velen would soon leave himself open to attack.
sources: DB: naga flag object 181694 at Traitor's Cove (posarea 3579)

parts.body: Confronted on the beach, the gnome fought to the death. The letter he carried, from Kael'thas himself, told of an eredar agent, still unknown to the draenei, who had revealed the Exodar's location, and called for a full assault to take back the ship. The admiral judged that the news must reach the king and the draenei leaders.

The letter went on to Exarch Menelaous at Azure Watch, who cursed them all to the Nether: a spy had been watching everything the draenei did. He took the warning to Velen, and bade the messenger stand ready for the Prophet's instructions.

title: The Promised One
body: At Azure Watch, Cryptographer Aurren has found that the language of the Stillpine furbolgs is carved into their totems, and Arugoo of the Stillpine waits beside the first of them. Following the totems one by one, up a hill, across the Crystalbrook and down to the riverbed, a reader learns the tongue until it reads like their own, and the last of them stands in Bristlelimb Village, where the Bristlelimb keep Stillpine furbolgs in cages. The carvings tell of a war between the two tribes, of terrible deeds done to the Stillpine, and of a prophecy: a hero not of furbolg blood will rise to save them.
notes: Converted: the opening keeps the totem trail and the prophecy carved on them (quest 9544 description). The rescue and the Promised One named moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9544); the blood crystal to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9565 or QUEST_ACCEPT 9566); the Kurken to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9570); Oomooroo and the raiders' charge to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 9573, a separate branch through 9562); the hold saved and the visions to part 5 (QUEST_DONE 9622, which needs only 9570). Before: Verified; 'the last totem points' fixed (Vark, the last, stands in the village) and the invented 'first sign' reworded. Faction 1. Check: part 1 trimmed to what turning in 9544 shows (the Promised One name and the road north are 9559's, now told in part 2, whose triggers need 9559). Part 4 no longer quotes creature_text 17445, which nothing in 3.3.5 makes him say (no SmartAI or script); it rests on 9573's reward text. Part 5: the core and O'ros are told as Menelaous hears them (9622 reward), not as the chief's reason for his warning.

parts.body: Those freed from the Bristlelimb cages hailed their rescuer, crying that the prophecy was true, and back at Azure Watch Arugoo humbled himself before the hero whose coming the spirits themselves had heralded. The prophecy of Akida, he said, had delivered a hero to the Stillpine.

Named the Promised One and sent north to Stillpine Hold, the hero found it overrun by maddened wildkin, and deep inside lay the root of the trouble: a crystal of the Exodar, blood red and dissolving into the cave's water, its sickly aura perhaps the cause of the savagery spreading across Azuremyst.
sources: quest 9559 description and reward text (Promised One, go north)

parts.body: Within the hold the Kurken, the beast of myth that came with the wildkin and slew so many Stillpine, was slain as Kurz the Revelator had foreseen, and the seer declared the prophecy nearly complete.

Deeper in the hold, Chieftain Oomooroo of the crazed wildkin fell. Stillpine the Younger, whose defenders had never managed to fight their way inside, saw the opening he had waited for and sent an attack into the hold at once.

With the hold saved, the Stillpine could return to their ancestral home. The high chief pledged his tribe's aid to the Promised One and warned that darkness waited for the draenei too. When the tale reached Exarch Menelaous, it was the visions that puzzled him most: the Stillpine had seen the power core of the Exodar, and the naaru O'ros.

title: All That Remains
body: On Silvermyst Isle, off the southwest coast of Azuremyst, the night elf fisherman Cowlen lived for years with his wife and daughter by the docks on the island's southeastern shore, at peace with the owlbeasts around them. Several weeks ago that peace ended. Owlbeasts maddened by the crystals that fell from the Exodar stormed the beach with murlocs beside them and fell upon the family, and the home they had made there was destroyed. Deranged owlbeasts still fill Moonwing Den in the island's heart.
sources: quests 10428, 9527, 9528 descriptions, reward and completion texts
npc_text of Cowlen 17311 (broken man, take my life)
notes: Converted: the opening now serves both entry points (ACCEPT 10428 at Dulvi, ACCEPT 9528 from Magwin herself), so it tells the attack both reveal (quests 9527, 9528) and neither Cowlen's survival nor Magwin's. The priestess's dreams moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 10428); Cowlen found to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 10428 or QUEST_ACCEPT 9527); the reunion to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9528). Dialogue check: npc_text 8869, 8870 hold nothing from later builds. Before: Verified. Faction 1: both quests Alliance only. Check: Thalrisa and Magwin taken out of the opening: Thalrisa is named only in 9527's completion text and Magwin only when met (9528) or in that same text, so neither entry point shows them; Magwin is named in part 3. The southeast docks (10428 log text) keep the opening in range.

parts.body: Word of it reached Azure Watch in an unlikely way. In her fevered dreams the injured night elf priestess spoke of a fisherman, Cowlen, in some distress on Silvermyst Isle, and with so much else happening no one had looked into it. Dulvi, uneasy, asked a willing stranger to go.

Cowlen was found on the docks, a broken man. He had fought until he was beaten senseless, and woke to sand soaked red with blood, his home razed and his ship sunk; his wife and daughter, he believed, had been devoured. He begged the stranger to end his life. He wanted no vengeance, only his family's remains for a proper burial.

Yet his daughter, Magwin, had escaped. Lost for weeks and sure that both her parents were dead, she was led home through the thicket, and father and daughter were reunited on the shore. Weeping for joy, Cowlen gave her rescuer a night elf heirloom, a token of friendship, trust and love, and named that stranger family until the end of time.

title: The Draenei Call of Fire
body: When a young draenei shaman is ready to learn the ways of flame, Tuluun of Azure Watch sends them to Emberglade to face Temper, a fire elemental of great power. Temper has a trouble of his own. The crash of the Exodar drove one of his brethren, Hauteur, insane, and the fallen elemental now demands that the owlbeasts of Silvermyst Isle worship him, something no true elemental would ever do. The balance must be restored, and the shaman's first task is to win back the ritual torch that the crazed wildkin have carried into Stillpine Hold.
notes: Converted: the torch and the effigy plan moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9465); Hauteur's death and rebirth to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9467); the ashes and Velen's summons to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9468). 9461 stays free for the Exodar. Before: Verified. Retitled from 'Call of Fire' to keep it apart from the orc and troll Call of Fire chain (2983, 1524, 1527) reserved for the Barrens. 9462 is a real entry point (Sulaa in the Exodar, Farseer Javad in Ironforge, turned in to Tuluun) and is kept; 9461 (from Tuluun, turned in to Velen) stays free. Faction 1: both quests Alliance only.

parts.body: The torch is the mark of Hauteur's arrogance: a flame that never goes out. Flame is meant to consume what it burns and then die, Temper teaches, to be reborn another time. The torch must burn a while longer all the same, for with it the shaman can light the effigy the owlbeasts of Moonwing Den burn in Hauteur's honor, and when he answers, put the fallen elemental out of his misery.

Hauteur came to his effigy and was destroyed, and his ashes were carried back to Emberglade. Death is no ending for fire: in destroying Hauteur the shaman also saved him, and reborn from his ashes he now burns beside Temper, brighter than before.

Part of the ashes was set aside for the shaman's fire totem. Tuluun saw in the trial a cleansing fire of destruction and renewal, not unlike the tribulation the draenei themselves are undergoing. Yet before the totem could be made, word came that the Prophet himself had heard of the shaman's success and asked to see them.
